newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Dalai Lama urges Taiwan to accept China links.
newsitem.headline: Dalai Lama urges Taiwan to accept China links.

text.p: Tibet's exiled spiritual leader, the Dalai Lama, on Thursday urged Taiwan to accept close economic linkages with rival China but said the Taiwanese people ultimately should be able to choose their own fate.

Saying that issues of the economy and defence transcended a region's right to preserve its own culture, the Dalai Lama told reporters: "As far as the economy is concerned, there should no longer be any independent economy of one country. The economy is now a global economy. Therefore, some kind of close link with mainland China should be there. But ultimately it is up to the people, the Taiwan issue."

The Dalai Lama, briefing reporters at the end of a six-day stay, reiterated his desire to negotiate a settlement with communist China, which has kept his vast Himalayan homeland under tight control since the early 1950s.
"The Tibetan problem is neither good for Tibet nor for China," he said. "We must find a mutual solution."

The Tibetan Buddhist god-king said that despite some Tibetan opposition he was willing to accept for Tibet the "one country, two systems" of local autonomy under Chinese sovereignty that Beijing has proposed for both Hong Kong and Taiwan.

"I believe very much in the spirit of one country two systems," he said. "Some critics in the Tibet community question my position. Even my eldest brother expressed that my middle approach is actually selling Tibet's legitimate rights."
